extracted.subtask_description: Standards and directives for running a military command (logistics, finance, fortifications, intelligence, discipline) as expressed in Napoleon's and ministers' letters to General Marmont. Focus is on what commanders must do or avoid to keep an army effective and obedient to central authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fortify and arm key positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Obey explicit orders to fortify positions (Raguse, Stagno, Santa-Croce, Lésina, Knim, Castelnovo, Cattaro) and construct forts and batteries as directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works should be executed promptly and even night and day when ordered; trace a fort at specified positions (e.g., Poitevin to trace a fort at Stagno), cut presqu'ile as ordered, and provide sufficient armament (artillery pieces, affûts) so places can resist attack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure regular administration of army finances
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain regular, lawful handling of funds; do not take money from payers' funds for unauthorized purposes or 'force the caisse'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request credits from the minister when needed; only expend funds that have been put at your disposal by ministerial decree. Violations of the treasury are condemned; the payeur may be held responsible and recalled if accounts are irregular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request and document credits before extraordinary spending
rubrics_metrics.description: When expenditures are required for execution of orders (works, transports, special missions), ask the minister for credits; if unavailable, do not habitually take funds without authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the minister refuses, you must refrain from making the expenditure unless extreme necessity; when funds are taken, send complete accounts and inventories of persons and sums so the minister can regularize them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize troop welfare and health while economizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep hospitals functioning, minimize mortality, and reduce supply costs (example: reduce prices of provisions by ~30%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good administration includes ensuring few sick in hospital, low mortality, and pursuing economies in supplies while keeping troop well-being; these facts are part of justifying administrative decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide siege and garrison supplies promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure forts and garrisons (e.g., Lésina, Stagno) have appropriate siege supplies and provisions so they can sustain defense if blockaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not postpone storing of siege supplies; anticipate blockades and place provisions in advance; if local funds are not provided, obtain them through proper channels or document extraordinary measures taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and secure lines of communication and transport
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize routes for movement of men and materiel (use of land and sea routes, placement of Tartars for rapid transit, construction of pontoon bridges where rivers block communications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mix of mulets, small boats, bricks/frégates for sea transport; for powder to Corfou send by land and sea (e.g., 50 mulets × 2 barrels each = 100 barrels) and expect partial losses when running enemy cruisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure regular intelligence and reconnaissance
rubrics_metrics.description: Send agents and officers to survey key areas (Bérat, Scutari, Durazzo and Vallona gulfs) and place agents among local leaders (e.g., Monténégrins) to obtain local knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require croquis and mémoires from engineers/marins to know harbor approaches; have a resident agent near influential local ecclesiastics or chieftains; demand regular reporting (consul should write daily).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish regular contacts with allied garrisons (Corfou) and exchange officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain weekly/biweekly officer exchanges and reporting with Corfou to keep perfect knowledge of localities and coordinate operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send an officer at least every 15 days to Corfou and have General Berthier send one likewise; frequent movement of officers creates familiarity with terrain and improves coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and arm local populations appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ local peoples (Dalmates) for island and coastal defense; arm them with rifles and light artillery to guard islands and prevent enemy landings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute fusils to form national guards, provide two 6-pounder iron guns for islands — local auxiliaries can free regular French/Italian troops for other duties and help prevent insults/landings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveil and control local political bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent local senates or assemblies from corresponding with foreigners or delegating without assent; arrest principal members if necessary and seize registers to stop traitorous correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat any who correspond with the enemy as traitors and enforce harsh penalties (Napoleon explicitly: 'le premier qui tiendra une correspondance avec l'étranger sera considéré comme traître et passé par les armes'); alternatively, send leaders under surveillance to safe locations (Venice, Milan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide prompt reports and full documentation to superiors
rubrics_metrics.description: Render direct, detailed accounts of affairs, administration, expenditures, and measures taken; correspond directly with the minister of war on service matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not route all reports only via chief of staff if ministerial responsibility demands direct correspondence; include detailed statements and receipts so minister can judge administration; responsibility is not covered unless minister has been directly informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execute urgent engineering works when strategic necessity demands
rubrics_metrics.description: When strategic orders demand fortification or construction (to preserve a place or honor of troops), act rapidly even if funds are slow to arrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such works are ordered and funds are lacking, the commander may advance urgent sums to prevent imminent risk, but must document and justify the expense to the minister for later regularization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit assemblies and unsanctioned deputations
rubrics_metrics.description: Forbid local bodies from assembling to send deputies or make independent diplomatic gestures without the commander's assent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage or prevent deputations and use existing envoy channels; only allow departures of envoys with authorization from superior (e.g., Emperor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be economical in supplies and reduce procurement costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek to lower expense of victuals and supplies (examples given: meat reduced from 0.34 to ~0.223 francs, bread from 0.41 to 0.27–0.28), and reduce extraordinary allowances when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous supervision of contracts and markets can reduce prices by about 30%; the ordonnateur and administration must pursue regular economies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow orders to support allied ships and officers when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide assistance and occasional funds to allied (e.g., Russian) officers or squadrons present in the area as ordered by higher authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such payments, if ordered, are legitimate but must be recorded and later regularized through ministerial channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare defenses for possible superior enemy squadrons
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate arrival of enemy squadrons (12–15 ships) and ensure measures are in place to shelter friendly squadrons from superior forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report to superior whether such defensive measures are in place and what further preparations may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate transport mixtures and expect attrition
rubrics_metrics.description: When attempting to run supplies past an enemy cruise, send multiple small vessels (bricks/frégates); expect 3–4 out of 5 to succeed when each is heavily laden (e.g., 3,000 powder each).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversify routes and means (land mulets + coastal boats) to increase probability of successful delivery; document realized losses and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept ministerial oversight and consequent responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand that direct correspondence with the minister creates chains of responsibility: commanders must report directly to the minister for service matters and will remain accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write directly to the minister of war; even when writing to the Emperor, you cannot be relieved of minsterial reporting obligations. This makes relations more particular and frequent.
